items.stem: Complete the statement: The principal budget factor is …
options: the largest expense in the budget
the cash balance at the year end
the budgeted profit
the factor that limits the activities of the business and is budgeted first
items.answer: the factor that limits the activities of the business and is budgeted first

items.stem: Explain two benefits of involving departmental managers in setting budgets.
items.answer: Managers have detailed knowledge so budgets are more realistic; they are more motivated to achieve targets they helped set.

items.stem: Explain the term "budgetary slack" and why it may arise.
items.answer: Slack is deliberate overestimation of costs or underestimation of revenue so that targets are easier to achieve; it arises in participative budgeting when managers are judged against budgets.

items.stem: Equinox plc makes bicycles. Identify the principal budget factor and the maximum number of units that can be budgeted.
items.answer: Material: 8,333 units
items.markingKey: sales demand 11,000 units, machine hours 11,800 units, labour hours 9,133 units, material 8,333 units [2]; principal budget factor: material, 8,333 units [1]

items.answer: Machine hours: 6,700 units

items.stem: Meridian Ltd is preparing its cash budget. (a) Calculate the receipts from customers for July. (b) Explain why depreciation is excluded from the cash budget.
items.answer: (a) $56,250 (b) It is a non-cash expense; the cash outflow occurred when the asset was bought.

items.stem: Which is NOT a purpose of budgeting?
options: Coordinating departments
Controlling costs by comparison with actual results
Guaranteeing that the business will make a profit
Planning future activities
items.answer: Guaranteeing that the business will make a profit
items.markingKey: Purposes: planning, coordination, communication, control, motivation [1].

items.stem: Distinguish between incremental budgeting and zero-based budgeting.
items.answer: Incremental adjusts last year's budget for expected changes (quick but carries forward inefficiency); ZBB justifies every activity from zero (removes waste but time-consuming).
items.markingKey: Incremental defined + evaluation [1]; ZBB defined + evaluation [1] [2]

items.stem: Complete the statement: Budgeted production equals …
options: opening inventory + closing inventory
budgeted sales only
budgeted sales + closing inventory of finished goods − opening inventory of finished goods
budgeted sales − closing inventory + opening inventory
items.answer: budgeted sales + closing inventory of finished goods − opening inventory of finished goods
items.markingKey: Production = sales + closing FG − opening FG [1].

items.stem: Explain why a business may budget to hold closing inventory of finished goods.
items.answer: To meet unexpected demand and avoid lost sales; to allow smooth production; but inventory has holding costs.
items.markingKey: Buffer for demand [1]; smooth production/cost noted [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain how the functional budgets are linked to one another.
items.answer: The sales budget determines production; production determines materials usage, purchases and labour; all feed the cash budget and master budget.
items.markingKey: Sales → production [1]; production → materials/labour [1]; all → cash/master [1] [3]

items.answer: (a) $59,950 (b) It is a non-cash expense; the cash outflow occurred when the asset was bought.

items.stem: Osprey Ltd is preparing its cash budget. Budgeted sales: February $78,000, March $27,000, April $67,000, May $40,000, June $78,000. 20% of sales are for cash (customers receive a 2% cash discount), 50% are received in the month after sale and 30% two months after sale. Monthly wages $15,500, other expenses $4,000 paid in the month, depreciation $1,100 a month. A machine costing $14,000 will be paid for in May. The bank balance at the start of April is $15,000. items.answer: (a) It is a non-cash expense; the cash outflow occurred when the asset was bought. (b) Cash arrives a month earlier, improving liquidity, but total receipts fall by the discount; worthwhile if the overdraft cost saved exceeds the discount.

materials needed for production + closing materials inventory − opening materials inventory
production units × selling price

items.stem: A trainee at Quetzal plc calculated budgeted production as 8,500 − 750 + 950 = 8,700 units, where 8,500 is budgeted sales, 750 closing inventory and 950 opening inventory. Explain the error and calculate the correct figure.
items.answer: Closing inventory must be added (it has to be produced) and opening inventory deducted (already available). Production = 8,500 + 750 − 950 = 8,300 units.

items.stem: Which item does NOT appear in a cash budget?

items.stem: Explain why profit and cash budgets show different results.
items.answer: Profit uses accruals (credit sales/purchases, depreciation), whereas cash records timing of receipts and payments, including capital items and loans not in profit.

items.stem: Explain two actions a business could take if its cash budget shows a deficit.
items.answer: Arrange an overdraft or short-term loan; delay capital expenditure; chase receivables or offer discounts; negotiate longer credit from suppliers.

items.stem: Complete the statement: A flexible budget is …
options: the cash budget
a budget prepared for one level of activity only
a budget adjusted to the actual level of activity achieved
a budget that is never revised
items.answer: a budget adjusted to the actual level of activity achieved
items.markingKey: Flexed for actual output; variable costs change, fixed costs do not [1].

items.stem: Explain why comparing actual costs with a fixed (original) budget may be misleading.
items.answer: If actual output differs from budget, variable costs will naturally differ; a flexible budget compares like with like, showing true efficiency.
items.markingKey: Activity level differs [1]; flexed budget gives meaningful comparison [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain two behavioural problems of budgetary control.
items.answer: Budgets seen as pressure may demotivate; managers may build in slack or spend to avoid cuts; focus on short-term targets at the expense of quality.

items.answer: All other budgets depend on it; e.g. if sales demand limits activity, production, purchases and labour budgets are derived from the sales budget.

items.stem: At Meridian Ltd: "The production budget was prepared before the sales budget." Explain the weakness in this budgeting practice and recommend an improvement.
items.answer: Sales demand is usually the principal budget factor; production should follow the sales budget.

items.stem: Monarch plc makes kayaks. Next year: sales demand 9,500 units; machine hours available 7,300 (1 per unit); labour hours available 20,300 (3 per unit); material available 40,000 kg (5 kg per unit). Identify the principal budget factor and the maximum number of units that can be budgeted.
items.answer: Labour hours: 6,766 units
items.markingKey: sales demand 9,500 units, machine hours 7,300 units, labour hours 6,766 units, material 8,000 units [2]; principal budget factor: labour hours, 6,766 units [1]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Complete the statement: The labour budget is calculated from … (b) Complete the statement: The materials purchases budget (in kg) equals …
items.answer: (a) budgeted production × labour hours per unit × rate per hour (b) materials needed for production + closing materials inventory − opening materials inventory
items.markingKey: (a) Labour cost = production × hours × rate [1]. (b) Purchases = usage + closing − opening [1].

items.stem: A trainee at Ibis plc calculated budgeted production as 9,700 − 400 + 450 = 9,750 units, where 9,700 is budgeted sales, 400 closing inventory and 450 opening inventory. Explain the error and calculate the correct figure.
items.answer: Closing inventory must be added (it has to be produced) and opening inventory deducted (already available). Production = 9,700 + 400 − 450 = 9,650 units.

items.stem: Odyssey plc plans to produce 14,400 units. Each unit needs 2 direct labour hours, paid at $15 per hour. Prepare the direct labour budget in hours and $.

Monarch plc is preparing its cash budget. Budgeted sales: July $72,000, August $70,000, September $78,000, October $36,000, November $90,000. 10% of sales are for cash, 50% are received in the month after sale and 40% two months after sale. Purchases are made at a gross margin of 25% (purchases = cost of sales of the same month) and paid one month later. Monthly wages $18,000, other expenses $4,000 paid in the month, depreciation $3,600 a month. A machine costing $18,000 will be paid for in October. The bank balance at the start of September is $17,000. (a) Calculate the receipts from customers for October. (b) Evaluate the effect on cash if customers paying in the month after sale were offered a 2% discount to pay immediately instead.
items.answer: (a) $70,600 (b) Cash arrives a month earlier, improving liquidity, but total receipts fall by the discount; worthwhile if the overdraft cost saved exceeds the discount.

items.stem: Pinnacle Ltd set an original budget for 24,000 units at $30 each, variable cost $12 per unit and fixed costs $111,000. Actual results: 30,000 units sold, revenue $895,500, variable costs $391,370, fixed costs $112,500. The manager claims: "Profit is above budget, so cost control was good." (a) Calculate the original budget profit, the flexed budget profit and the actual profit. (b) Calculate the sales volume variance (original vs flexed profit) and the total flexible budget variance.
items.answer: (a) $321,000; $429,000; $391,630 (b) Volume $108,000 F; flexible budget variance $37,370 A

items.stem: Kestrel plc sells 20% of goods for cash and the rest on credit (40% paid one month later, 40% two months later). Sales were $54,000, $31,000, $39,000 for February, March, April. A trainee shows receipts of $39,000 for April, equal to April sales. Explain the error and calculate the correct receipts.
items.answer: Receipts depend on when customers pay, not when sales are made. Correct receipts for April = $41,800.
items.markingKey: Timing of credit receipts [1]; correct pattern applied [1]; $41,800 [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain why a business with a budgeted profit may still forecast an overdraft.
items.answer: Cash may be tied up in receivables and inventory, spent on non-current assets or loan repayments, or suppliers paid before customers pay.

items.stem: Budgeted sales: November $33,000, December $21,000, January $41,000, February $77,000, March $78,000. 20% of sales are for cash, 60% are received in the month after sale and 20% two months after sale. Purchases are made at a gross margin of 25% (purchases = cost of sales of the same month) and paid one month later. Monthly wages $14,500, other expenses $11,500 paid in the month, depreciation $3,300 a month. A machine costing $36,000 will be paid for in February. The bank balance at the start of January is $11,000. Calculate the receipts, the payments and the closing bank balance for January.
items.answer: Receipts $27,400; payments $41,750; closing balance -$3,350

items.stem: Quetzal plc is preparing its cash budget. Budgeted sales: March $46,000, April $64,000, May $73,000, June $67,000, July $60,000. 20% of sales are for cash (customers receive a 2.5% cash discount), 50% are received in the month after sale and 30% two months after sale. Purchases are made at a gross margin of 25% (purchases = cost of sales of the same month) and paid one month later. Monthly wages $16,000, other expenses $8,000 paid in the month, depreciation $1,600 a month. A machine costing $25,000 will be paid for in June. The bank balance at the start of May is $2,000. (a) Calculate the receipts from customers for June. (b) Explain why depreciation is excluded from the cash budget.
items.answer: (a) $68,765 (b) It is a non-cash expense; the cash outflow occurred when the asset was bought.

items.stem: Condor Ltd budgeted material costs of $95,000 for 9,500 units ($10 per unit). Actual output was 14,500 units and material cost $145,767. The production manager was criticised for an adverse variance of $50,767. Explain why this criticism may be unfair and calculate a fairer variance.
items.answer: The budget should be flexed to actual output: 14,500 × $10 = $145,000. Fair variance = $767 A.
items.markingKey: Fixed budget compares different activity levels [1]; flexed budget $145,000 [1]; variance $767 A [1] [3]

items.stem: Saffron plc budgeted to sell 25,500 units at $20 with variable costs per unit of materials $4 and labour $4, and fixed costs of $55,000. Actual sales were 21,700 units: revenue $434,000, materials $90,702, labour $93,702, fixed costs $57,000. Calculate the flexed budget profit and the total variance from it.
items.answer: Flexed profit $205,400; actual $192,596; variance $12,804 A
items.markingKey: Flexed at 21,700 units: revenue $434,000, materials $86,800, labour $86,800, fixed $55,000, profit $205,400 [2]; variances revenue $0 (nil), materials $3,902 A, labour $6,902 A, fixed costs $2,000 A [2]; total $12,804 A [1]

items.stem: Galaxy Ltd budgeted to sell 19,500 units at $25 with variable costs per unit of materials $5 and labour $6, and fixed costs of $79,000. Actual sales were 22,400 units: revenue $537,600, materials $107,262, labour $143,907, fixed costs $80,500. Prepare a flexible budget statement and calculate the variance for each item, labelling each F or A.
items.answer: Flexed profit $234,600; revenue $22,400 A, materials $4,738 F, labour $9,507 A, fixed costs $1,500 A; total $28,669 A
items.markingKey: Flexed at 22,400 units: revenue $560,000, materials $112,000, labour $134,400, fixed $79,000, profit $234,600 [2]; variances revenue $22,400 A, materials $4,738 F, labour $9,507 A, fixed costs $1,500 A [2]; total $28,669 A [1]
